profile.headline: Software Engineer at L3Harris, Maritime Systems
profile.summary:
SWE of maritime defense systems, but open-minded and adaptable to new technologies. Great at learning new skills through Google, YouTube, reading, and now AI. Satisfied by solving problems, especially through programming. Always seeking ways to improve myself. 

Fun Facts

Favorite Programming Language: Python because of its simplicity and wide array of libraries. Java is a close second because of nostalgia.

Least Favorite Programming Language: JavaScript. Its syntax feels like an awkward mix between Python and Java, being weakly typed like Python but requiring boilerplate keywords like Java. While I respect JavaScript's rise from frontend to full stack, I'm not a fan of its syntax.

Favorite Operating System: Ubuntu because it offers the flexibility of Linux and has an active community on Ask Ubuntu. For aesthetics, I enjoy Archcraft Linux.

Favorite Version Control System: Git because it's satisfying to use from the terminal, well-integrated with GitHub and Bitbucket, and fast. 

Favorite Relational Database: SQLite. I appreciate its ease of use for developing personal projects. If I had to pick a relational DB for a production environment, I'd choose PostgreSQL, but I don't think it matters that much.

Favorite NoSQL Database: Redis because it excels in simplicity and speed. I like my databases the same way I like my programming languages/everything in life: simple.

Favorite AI Coding Assistant: Codex, for now... although OpenAI and Anthropic keep leapfrogging each other.

positions.title: Software Engineer, Sr. Associate
positions.description:
Primary developer of a Condition Based Monitoring (CBM) internal research project. Using PySpark and Palantir Foundry, I’ve developed a data pipeline that discovers ship machinery states via clustering. I've contributed to all stages of the pipeline: ingest, unzip, normalize, feature engineer, and cluster. I've also developed tools for exploratory data analysis and visualization. The current phase of the project is fault discovery, but this will eventually extend to real-time fault prediction.

Also primary developer of the Machinery Centralized Control System (MCCS), On-Board Training System (OBTS) for the next generation US Navy frigate (FFG-62). I develop machinery plant simulations to train control system operators. I collaborate with controls engineers to create realistic simulations and useful instructor capabilities, like save states and dashboards for introducing faults. I've improved the build process by creating a Jenkins pipeline that builds + packages multiple repositories into a single zip file. Using Java and Redis, I’ve simulated electrical, propulsion, auxiliary, and damage control systems for the frigate. The electrical system is particularly polished: it includes diesel generators that distribute voltage + frequency, connect to load centers via breakers, and can be commanded to receive different base loads when run in parallel. I’ve also simulated components of the combined diesel-electric and gas propulsion system, including the dual-redundant Modbus TCP behavior.

positions.title: Intern D, Software Engineering
positions.description:
Developed quality-of-life features and improvements for an automated integration testing app. Features include the parsing of two input files: a spreadsheet with expected run times for each test, and a text file of tests to run. The spreadsheet was used to display expected vs actual runtimes, which is useful for engineers debugging the system. The text file was used to limit unnecessary tests from running.

Optimized the build process of an old control system, making it easier for oncoming engineers to understand. Using Java, Batch, and PowerShell, I added safety checks for duplicate VM instances that could break the build. Similar to the project above, I enabled the build GUI to parse a spreadsheet and display expected vs actual times for various build steps.

Wrote regression test procedures based on customer’s software design instructions.

positions.title: Intern C, Software Engineering
positions.description:
Developed maritime Intelligence/Surveillance/Reconnaissance (ISR) and sonar programs. Both programs used an agile workflow with Atlassian to manage sprints and Git to manage version control.

For the ISR program, I created and edited various panels on the frontend and added threads to poll for input USB devices like joystick controllers. This was done in Java and JavaFX.

For the sonar program, I helped refactor the old codebase using static analysis tools. I pair programmed directly with the other developers and provided moral support :) This was done in C++.

volunteerExperiences.description: I volunteer at the warehouse and market of a local food pantry. At the warehouse, I stock shelves and process donated items. At the market, I help clients choose their groceries.

As a mentor, I spend time around kids who are at risk (have been through the juvenile court system) at events, like trips to amusement parks and local attractions. I socialize with the kids and try to set a positive example.
